QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_50

question.text: Mr. Arjun Reddy, ops head at Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (close-ended 6-year Cat III), is preparing for the tenure-end. Liquid positions are 82% of NAV; 18% remains illiquid at month -3. The optimal playbook is to:

answer.text: Sell illiquid positions at any price before tenure end
Enter the 1-year Liquidation Period; attempt 25%-bid arrangement; if unresolved, seek 75% consent for Dissolution Period filing via merchant banker
Extend tenure unilaterally by 2 years without investor consent
Transfer illiquid positions to the IM's proprietary book

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Correct playbook: enter the 1-year Liquidation Period on tenure expiry; during this window, attempt bid-arrangement (minimum 25% of illiquid value) and in-specie distribution (with 75% consent); if the 1-year runs out, file merchant-banker Information Memorandum + Due Diligence Certificate BEFORE expiry to enter Dissolution Period (subject to 75% investor consent). Dissolution Period cannot exceed ORIGINAL tenure. **The Trap:** Fire-sale (A) destroys value and creates mis-selling risk. Unilateral extension (C) requires 2/3-by-value consent. Transfer to IM book (D) is a related-party transaction breaching fiduciary duty. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C/D test the same Liquidation/Dissolution Period pathway. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Build the tenure-exit calendar 18 months before tenure-end: month -18 start liquidity plan; month -6 valuer appointments; month -3 LP consent drives; month 0 enter Liquidation Period; month +9 start Dissolution filing if needed. Skipping the calendar triggers Re. 1 in-specie — reputational death.
